dimension_justifications.soundness: The central descriptive readout is plausible and the paper is unusually candid about its scope, pairing, post-treatment amendment, weak cells, and failed original calibration. However, all numeric evidence is source-reported and locally unverifiable, the active-block claim lacks the decisive same-trajectory recorder control, the partition intervention is confounded with allocation, the full selector lacks arm-level and family-wise null calibration, and the development/probe sequence does not provide an independent held-out replication.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The manuscript is anonymous, readable, visually intact, and within the nine-page main-text limit; it clearly distinguishes stability from false-positive control and description from mechanism. Evaluation is nevertheless burdened by dense appendix bookkeeping, inferential-looking rank-sum z values whose dependence treatment is unclear, and many provenance paths that point to absent artifacts.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The recorder-relative measurement warning and two-layer reachability-versus-magnitude reporting rule are useful, but the contribution remains a narrow case study on one private checkpoint, one task, one question pool, and one composite schedule intervention. Without a dual-recorder or factorial control and independent replication, it does not establish a mechanism or broadly validated diagnostic.

paper_summary: The paper studies identity-lock-time periodicity for a blockwise-decoded LLaDA-style model observed through an active-block recorder. On three canvas-256 arms and two separately registered canvas-96 probes, a pre-treatment min-max candidate selector and a rank-sum comparison return the configured block length; paired question bootstraps report stable selection. The paper also reports negative candidate-32 readouts, a post-data spectral residual check, and a separate content-confidence association. It explicitly frames these as recorder-relative descriptive and stability evidence, not a null-calibrated detection result or model-mechanism claim.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest verifiable contribution in the snapshot is the disciplined experimental accounting and claim boundary: the manuscript specifies the paired question design, resampling budgets and several seeds, exposes boundary cardinalities, documents the post-treatment scope amendment and anti-conservative original gate, and consistently limits the headline to recorder-relative selection. The reported experimental values themselves remain cannot_verify because their event streams, results, code, and checkpoint are absent.
strengths: The joint cluster bootstrap reapplies one shared question-index draw across arms, preserving the intended cross-arm pairing instead of treating five marginals as independent.
The manuscript correctly distinguishes bootstrap selection stability from a false-positive rate and reports the registered criterion's weaker 0.8805 positivity on the reused L32 control.

Registration history is unusually transparent: estimator development on the control, the post-treatment withdrawal of the model-intrinsic branch, and later preregistration of the non-nested probes are disclosed rather than collapsed into a single confirmatory story.

The original selectivity gate's 10/25 wrong-candidate failure is reported, and the corrected margin, cross-condition red-team, L24 marginal result, and absence of full selector calibration are explicitly bounded.
Boundary-set cardinalities, including the single-locus L48 estimate, are printed, and the paper does not treat the spectral negative as ruling out arbitrary residual shapes.
Execution budgets, question counts, NFE schedules, decoder seed, bootstrap/permutation budgets, environment versions, and the private-checkpoint boundary are reported.
questions: Are the exact same 300 GSM8K items, in the same item-to-canvas assignment, used in all five arms, including the pre-existing L32 pool and canvas-96 probes? Please provide the frozen item IDs, order, assignment rule, and digest.

Which analyses were fixed before the L16/L64 data, which were added after those data, and which were fixed only before the canvas-96 probes? In particular, were the corrected margin null, rank-sum comparator, DFT family, and cross-arm summary preregistered?

How are the Mann-Whitney z values in Table 2 calibrated given that adjacent differences share positionwise medians, neighboring d(r) values overlap, and positions within an arm are serially dependent?

What is the empirical family-wise type-I error and power of the complete procedure, including candidate selection, five arms, and any outcome-dependent follow-up analyses, under a clean structured null?

Can the same generated trajectories be logged simultaneously by active-block and passive/full-canvas recorders, and can partition and per-block allocation be varied factorially without changing the target NFE budget?

issues.location: Snapshot evidence/repository_inventory.md; evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv; evidence/experiment_registry.json; evidence/method_provenance.tsv; manuscript Appendix A.3 Table 9 (p.13) and Appendix B (p.18)
issues.observed_evidence: The inventory states that every named results JSON and analysis script is not located; the claim map marks all central numeric claims source_reported/cannot_verify_locally; the registry marks X1-X2 reported_not_rerun; and each method implementation is manuscript-specified only or has no located code. The PDF likewise says the event streams, scripts, evidence ledgers, and private checkpoint are not included.
issues.why_it_matters: No reported separation, bootstrap fraction, rank-sum value, permutation result, sample identity, or registration chronology can be independently recomputed from the frozen review evidence. This is a cannot_verify finding rather than evidence that the values are false, but it imposes a hard ceiling on soundness confidence.
issues.required_fix: Provide a blind, hash-pinned supplement containing the preregistrations and amendments, frozen item IDs, immutable event streams or sufficient derived data, all result files, analysis scripts, environments, and exact commands. If the private checkpoint cannot be released, include releasable events plus a public-checkpoint replication or clearly declare the irreducible boundary.
issues.verification_test: From a clean environment, recompute Tables 2-12 and Figure 2 from the supplied events; require exact or tolerance-declared agreement, verify every digest against Table 9, and independently check the preregistration timestamps and analysis-to-claim mapping.
issues.evidence_needed: Frozen preregistration records, item/pool manifest, event streams, result JSONs, analysis and figure scripts, environment lock, execution logs, and checkpoint identity or a public replication.

issues.location: Section 2, Matched intervention and scope (p.3, lines 173-178); Section 4 (p.8, lines 395-404); evidence/experiment_registry.json entries A31-X3 and A31-X4
issues.observed_evidence: Changing block length changes both partition geometry and the required per-block step allocation. No uniform-allocation or partition-by-allocation factorial arm was run, and no identical trajectory was recorded through both active-block and passive/full-canvas instruments. The registry marks both decisive controls not_run.
issues.why_it_matters: The experiment identifies an association between a composite schedule and an active-recorder output, but it cannot determine whether observed periodicity is created by recorder visibility, sampler-state dynamics, allocation, or their interaction. This directly limits the causal force and generality of the reporting recommendation.
issues.required_fix: Run a preregistered same-trajectory dual-recorder comparison and the smallest feasible partition-by-allocation factorial design, preserving model, question assignment, canvas, NFE, and decode randomness. Treat any infeasible cell explicitly and restrict claims to identifiable contrasts.
issues.verification_test: Verify bit-identical underlying trajectories across recorder modes, then estimate paired contrasts for period selection and magnitude. In the factorial run, test partition, allocation, and interaction effects with cluster-aware uncertainty and demonstrate that the claimed recorder-relative effect persists when allocation is controlled.
issues.evidence_needed: Dual-recorder event streams, factorial schedules, paired item/seed manifest, prespecified contrasts, interaction estimates, and execution logs.

issues.location: Section 3.1 and Table 5 (pp.5-6); Appendix A.5 and Table 10 (p.14); evidence/experiment_registry.json entry A31-X5
issues.observed_evidence: The original threshold flags 10/25 wrong candidates. The corrected top-minus-second margin gives per-arm exact p-values and four nominal values below 0.05, but the paper concedes that this is neither an arm-level false-positive-rate estimate nor family-wise calibration of the complete candidate-selection procedure. No structured arm-level null with family-wise calibration was run.
issues.why_it_matters: Bootstrap mode fractions answer sample stability, not whether the selector would find schedule-aligned periods under a scientifically relevant null. Reporting four arms as reaching 5% significance across five arms and a candidate search without a complete multiplicity calibration can overstate evidential strength, especially after the original gate failed badly.
issues.required_fix: Freeze a scientifically justified structured null that preserves nuisance trends and dependence, apply the entire selection and follow-up pipeline to each null replicate, and control the maximum statistic across candidates, arms, and prespecified follow-ups. Label post-selected checks exploratory.
issues.verification_test: On known-null simulations and clean negative arms, estimate family-wise error with a confidence interval and require compatibility with the declared alpha; on injected alternatives spanning the observed boundary cardinalities, report power and selection accuracy. Re-evaluate all headline language under the calibrated threshold.
issues.evidence_needed: Full-pipeline null generator, preregistered multiplicity family, null and injected-alternative replicates, FWER/power estimates, and code.

issues.location: Table 1 and Section 2 (pp.2-3); Appendix A.2 Table 8 (p.12); Section 3.2 (p.7); Appendix B (p.18)
issues.observed_evidence: All arms use one fixed 300-question pool and one private checkpoint. The L32 arm is a reused contiguous development subset on which the estimator was selected after a failed score; the non-nested probes were registered only after the main treatment data; and no fresh held-out L32 replication or cross-seed/model/task replication was run. The paired bootstrap resamples this same pool and cross-seed variance is excluded from the estimand.
issues.why_it_matters: Pairing efficiently estimates within-pool schedule differences but does not repair adaptive reuse of the development arm, purposive or order-dependent pool selection, or the absence of independent replication. Near-perfect bootstrap stability can coexist with poor transport beyond this fixed pool and trajectory configuration.
issues.required_fix: Predeclare a held-out item sample and item-assignment rule, run a fresh L32 control and the complete arm set without estimator changes, and repeat across enough decode seeds or deterministic replays to establish the intended stochastic target. At minimum, separate development, post-main-data probe, and confirmatory evidence in every aggregate claim.
issues.verification_test: Confirm zero overlap with estimator-development data, reproduce P*=L and calibrated margins on the held-out sample, and show robustness across paired seeds or bitwise deterministic replays. Report between-sample and between-run variation rather than only resampling the original pool.
issues.evidence_needed: Pool construction and item-order provenance, held-out IDs, fresh-arm outputs, paired seed schedule or replay audit, and a frozen analysis plan.

issues.location: Section 2, non-extremal robustified comparison (p.4, lines 162-167); Table 2 (p.4); Figure 2 discussion (p.5)
issues.observed_evidence: The paper reports Mann-Whitney rank-sum z values over boundary and interior d(r) values and treats their argmax as an independent robustification, but it does not state how the calculation accounts for the strong dependence induced by shared positionwise medians, overlapping adjacent differences, serial position structure, unequal boundary counts, and reused decodes. The implementation artifact is not located.
issues.why_it_matters: A conventional rank-sum z calibration assumes observations with independence properties that these position-derived values do not obviously satisfy. If uncorrected, the large z values are inferentially misleading and the comparator is not independent evidence because it is computed from the same profiles.
issues.required_fix: Define the exact statistic and its estimand, avoid inferential z language unless calibrated, and use a decode-cluster-aware or structure-preserving randomization/bootstrap that recomputes medians and adjacent differences within each replicate. Describe the comparator as a sensitivity analysis on the same data.
issues.verification_test: Under simulated and empirical structured nulls with the observed position dependence and boundary cardinalities, verify type-I error of the reported rank-sum procedure; then recompute its uncertainty by resampling decode clusters and confirm whether L remains the maximizing candidate.
issues.evidence_needed: Rank-sum implementation, replicate-level d(r) construction, dependence-preserving null simulations, calibrated uncertainty, and the full per-arm outputs.

issues.location: Table 3 (p.6); Section 3.2 (p.7); Appendix A.1 Table 7 (p.11); Section 4 (p.8)
issues.observed_evidence: The L48 positive separation rests on one boundary locus, L24 fails its corrected margin test, and the DFT power check covers only one sinusoidal residual-32 family on L16. The paper acknowledges these facts and phrases the negative as not revealing a recorder-observable fixed-32 component rather than proving absence.
issues.why_it_matters: The negative evidence has low and highly shape-specific power, so it cannot support broader absence, universality, or strong boundary-margin claims. The current wording is mostly responsible, but the five-arm synthesis can still make the evidence look more uniform than it is.
issues.required_fix: Keep single-locus and marginal arms separate in headline summaries, report a prospective power/sensitivity envelope for each negative family, and avoid aggregating them as equivalent confirmations. Add more boundary repetitions or larger canvases if stronger exclusion is desired.
issues.verification_test: For each arm and residual family, simulate injected effects across shape and amplitude, report detection probability with uncertainty, and show that any retained negative claim is limited to amplitudes and shapes with adequate power.
issues.evidence_needed: Arm-specific injected-signal power curves, larger-canvas or replicated-boundary probes, and prespecified exclusion thresholds.

ethics_concerns: No material ethics issue is identifiable from the frozen snapshot. The private checkpoint and unreleased artifacts are transparency and reproducibility concerns rather than an evident ethics violation; GSM8K use and AI-assisted preparation are disclosed.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A complete, hash-pinned artifact supplement that reproduces all tables and figures and verifies the registration chronology.
A same-trajectory active-versus-passive recorder experiment demonstrating the measurement-window effect directly.
A partition-by-allocation factorial control that separates geometry, step allocation, and interaction effects at fixed NFE.
Full-pipeline structured-null calibration controlling multiplicity across candidates, arms, and prespecified follow-ups, with adequate power.
A fresh held-out replication, including an independent L32 control and additional paired seeds or deterministic replays, showing stable results beyond the development pool.
Dependence-aware calibration of the rank-sum sensitivity analysis.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Recomputation from raw events fails to match the reported separations, bootstrap fractions, p-values, or artifact hashes.
A full-pipeline null audit shows materially inflated family-wise false positives or strong preference for candidates with few boundaries.
A dual-recorder control shows the same apparent periodicity under a passive/full-canvas instrument, contradicting the recorder-window interpretation.
A factorial run attributes the effect primarily to per-block allocation or an uncontrolled interaction rather than partition/observability.
Fresh held-out arms or paired-seed reruns fail to select the configured block length, especially for the weak L24, L48, or L32 cells.
The claimed shared-question pairing or preregistration chronology cannot be substantiated.
review_limitations: All central experimental measurements are author-reported and cannot be independently recomputed because the referenced artifacts are absent.
The review was confined to the frozen submission snapshot and did not inspect repository history, prior reviews, author plans, outside literature, or target scores.
Citation support was assessed only through the included partial citation lock; novelty and literature verification were not independently performed.
